strings.name: Nelson Mandela
strings.role: Leader in South Africa’s democratic transition · Nobel Peace Prize laureate
strings.summary: Mandela developed from a lawyer and African National Congress activist into a leading figure in South Africa’s anti-apartheid movement. After armed resistance and a long imprisonment, he joined negotiations to end white-minority rule. He shared the 1993 Nobel Peace Prize with F. W. de Klerk and became president after democratic elections the following year. After one term, he stepped down and continued work in philanthropy and social reconciliation.
strings.coverageNote: Selected milestones from 1918 to 2013, compiled from Nelson Mandela Foundation archival material and Nobel Prize summaries.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-01.value: Mvezo, Eastern Cape region, South Africa
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: BA, University of South Africa; LLB from the same university in 1989
strings.facts.fact-03.label: Presidential term
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Helping end apartheid
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: After his release, took part in political negotiations and worked with others to advance South Africa’s transition to democracy.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: 1993 Nobel Peace Prize
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Shared the award with F. W. de Klerk for work toward peacefully ending apartheid and establishing a democratic South Africa.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: First president of democratic South Africa
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: Took office in 1994 after the first non-racial national democratic elections and stepped down after one term in 1999.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Dies in Johannesburg
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Died at home aged 95. His struggle against apartheid and work toward reconciliation became an important historical legacy.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Steps down and establishes a foundation
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Kept his promise to serve only one term and established the Nelson Mandela Foundation to continue his public work.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Becomes president of democratic South Africa
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Sworn in after South Africa’s first non-racial national democratic elections.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Shares the Nobel Peace Prize
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Awarded jointly with de Klerk for their efforts to end apartheid and advance the democratic transition.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Released after long imprisonment
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Joined formal negotiations to end white-minority rule and was elected ANC president in 1991.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Sentenced to life imprisonment
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Received a life sentence in the Rivonia Trial, followed by long imprisonment on Robben Island and elsewhere.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Helps establish Umkhonto we Sizwe
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Went underground after the ANC was banned and helped create the armed organization Umkhonto we Sizwe.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Leads the Defiance Campaign and practices law
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Helped lead a campaign against discriminatory laws and opened a law practice with Oliver Tambo.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Helps found the ANC Youth League
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Joined the African National Congress and established its Youth League with fellow activists, entering anti-apartheid politics.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Mvezo
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in the Eastern Cape region; later studied at Fort Hare and the University of South Africa, among other institutions, and entered law.
